This receipt originally concluded that was NOT a guard loss, on two grounds that are both still true: the two .githooks directories were byte-identical (`diff -rq` reported no differences), and .githooks/pre-push resolves the tree it gates from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` against PWD at push time rather than from the hook's own location. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 before this receipt was ever pushed: that conclusion was wrong by the project's own standard. scripts/hookspath-fleet-guard.test.mjs failed this folder on the first carrier push -- "this checkout HAS its own .githooks/pre-push, but core.hooksPath points past it" -- and that guard, not my reasoning, is the authority. Byte-identical today does not make a checkout self-sufficient: git skips a missing or unrunnable hook silently, so if the main checkout's copy were ever moved or changed, a push from here would look identical to a pass. The config was repointed with the exact command the guard prescribes, `git config --worktree core.hooksPath .githooks`, on this checkout only; no other worktree's config was touched, which stays owner-hands. The guard then passed 39/39.
